Home Hijackings 2

By: Graham Coetzer | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Homeowners and landlords across the country are struggling to evict illegal tenants - has the law failed them?

Unique Selling Point:
Two oceans marathon winner Thulani Sibisi bought a house in Orlando in the same street where Walter Sisulu once lived. It was his dream to live out his last days next to where the famous SA icon once lived. But since buying his property four years ago, Thulani has never been able to occupy the home. A family member of the previous owner has occupied the house and refused to move. Despite four court ordered evictions, police have failed to keep the illegal tenants out. We accompanied Thulani, the Sherrif and Public order policing units to serve the fourth eviction. But the tenant gathered support from the local community, and was able to break back into the house the very same day, chasing away Thulani's private security firm and reoccupying the home. Police stood by and did nothing despite our camera's presence.

Summary:
Thulani's plight highlights the failure of the justice system to protect homeowners once tenants illegally occupy a home. Meanwhile, homeowners from our previous story in Eveleigh Estate in Boksburg, which dealt with the same issue, have still not had any successes either. After our story aired, most of the houses forcefully evicted by members of the EFF were reoccupied by the same tenants. Even landlords in upmarket areas face similar battles. Michelle Dickens from the TPN Credit Bureau monitors tenant behaviour in SA. She says 10% of tenants in SA are more than 3 months in arrears in South Africa. According to their data, problem tenants are in two categories - low end tenants who pay rental of R3000 per month and less, and high end tenants, who pay rental of more than R12 000. She has provided us with a landlord, Caroline, who is willing to be interviewed on the battles she has faced in getting tenants evicted in Up market Johannesburg suburbs. I am just waiting for her to contact me back, but Michelle has confirmed she will do interview.

Press Release:


Eviction Nightmares
Homeowners and landlords across the country are struggling to evict illegal tenants – but has the law failed them? Carte Blanche investigates why four court-ordered evictions have not been enough to get illegal, non-paying tenants out of marathon runner Thulani Sibisi’s dream home. Now a Gauteng-based attorney is fighting to change the law that currently appears to favour tenants rather than property owners.
Producer: Graham Coetzer
Presenter: Derek Watts


Script:


Eviction Nightmares
15 November 2018

Voice
This is Thulani Sibisi, a former marathon star and long distance running olympic coach. Today’s athletes can make millions from their victories, but that wasn’t the case in Sibisi’s time and he says he’s now running on empty.

Sound Up Thulani
Derek: Thulani, did running make you rich? What did you get for winning the 1986 Two Oceans?

Thulani: Sjoe, rich? I got R250.

Derek: R250.

Thulani: Yes. It couldn’t pay even my flight.

Link Derek
The winner of the 1986 Two Ocean’s marathon, Thulani Sibisi, lives in a back room of this house in Soweto. Four years ago he sank his life savings into what he saw as his dream house for retirement.

Voice
But instead of living in this house he paid R460 000 for, which is on the same street as the Sisulu family home in Orlando, Soweto, Sibisi is now stuck in this small room with all his possessions.

Sound Up Thulani Sibisi
Baba Walter Sisulu is my hero, as well as mama Albertina is my hero. And I said you know what, that’s the house, I couldn’t even change my mind, I said this is the house.

Voice
Four years after buying his dream home, Sibisi, who has been diagnosed with stage three prostate cancer, has hardly ever set foot in it. Before he could move in, a family member of the deceased previous owner, Nokuthula Zwane, occupied it and refused to leave.

Sound Up Thulani
They said I am not going to live there, so if I want to be killed, so I must try to come and stay there.

Voice
Attorney Cilna Steyn is a panel expert on evictions for the Law Society of South Africa. She specialises in home hijackings and delinquent tenants.

Sound Up Cilna
Derek: Cilna, would you say defaulting tenants are on the rise in South Africa?

Cilna: not just defaulting tenants, truly delinquent tenants. The main concern is the tenants who really just don’t pay. And in the current economy, we’ve seen a steep increase in that.

Voice
In July this year we brought you the shocking story of Eveleigh Estate, a suburban townhouse complex in Boksburg. Here, homeowners like Shimi Mahlaela were at war with delinquent tenants who were not paying their rent.

Sound Up Shimi Mahlaela
At the moment, I’m owing more than a million in levies and rates and taxes. I’ve lost half a million in legal fees.



Voice
To make matters worse, the complex had become known as crime-central as the delinquent tenants dealt drugs, waged gang wars and vandalised the property. Things came to a head when homeowners, residents, and ironically members of the EFF decided to forcefully evict the tenants.

Sound Up Fighting

Voice
Mahlaela had gone to court to try and get eviction orders for the three units he owns. When we spoke to him earlier this week, he said nothing had changed at Eveleigh.

Sound Up Shimi Mahlaela
While we are going the eviction route, the guys are not paying anything towards rental, towards electricity. They are not paying for water, and we are responsible to pay the bond and the rates

Link Derek
Our previous story was just the tip of the iceberg. Homeowners and landlords across the country face similar problems. Defaulting tenants are on the rise, and it could happen to you.

Voice
Caroline Czuba says she fell victim to a delinquent tenant when she rented out an apartment she had inherited from her mother in Sandton.

Sound Up Caroline
Caroline: Well it was a very presentable lady, who seemed very educated, well spoken. She told me she had a christian background with very high moral values… It didn’t turn out like that.

Derek:But very soon afterward she stopped paying?

Caroline: After one month that was it, and she never paid again.

Voice
Whether it’s a home hijacking like in Sibisi’s case, or a delinquent tenant who targets landlord’s like Czuba, you’re in trouble. Your only option is to go to court and get an eviction order - and it’s going to cost you time and money. But as Sibisi found out, even a court ordered eviction is not always enough.

Sound Up Cilna Steyn
Well this is the fourth time we have executed.

Voice
Sibisi has been lucky enough to receive financial assistance for his case from both the real estate agency who sold him the house and friends like Comrades Marathon legends Johnny Halberstadt and Bob de la Motte. Cilna Steyn was successful in obtaining an eviction order in the South Gauteng High Court. But during the first three evictions, community members in Orlando assisted Nokuthula Zwane in preventing the evictions.

Sound Up Cilna Steyn
By the evening, at 9 o clock, the security guard in the premises called me, and said the community are starting to burn items outside the house.





Voice
Two weeks ago we accompanied Steyn on the fourth eviction. Present was a sizeable force made up of members of the Public Order Policing Unit, a Private security firm, the Sheriff of the court and team, as well as the Ombudsman for the Department of Human Settlements Themba Mthetwa. Sibisi was also in attendance, determined to finally take occupation.

Sound Up Thulani Sibis
I will stay there in my house. If they have to kill me in my house, let it be so. Be killed in my own house that I’ve paid for.

Voice
Armed to the teeth and prepared for trouble, the convoy set off to Sibisi’s home, where the Sheriff served the eviction order on Zwane, who claimed she had full rights to live in the house.

Sound Up Thulani
She says she has an order, court order, that says she could stay here.

Voice
But Zwane was unable to produce the document, so the sheriff went ahead with the eviction. The process entails members of the sheriffs office removing every single item found inside the property. Human Settlements Ombud Themba Mthethwa has tried convincing the local community to allow the law to take its course.

Sound Up Themba Mthetwa
I met the ward councillors, I met people from the Gauteng legislature to come and help us, and speak to the community, and allow the owner to move in.

Voice
But it was soon obvious that his pleas had fallen on deaf ears, as Zwane was already calling in her reinforcements and threatening Sibisi despite the heavy police presence.

Sound Up Thulani
I’m scared, because after this I don’t know what will happen. But I can’t run away, it’s my house, how do I run away?

Voice
Sibisi says Zwane is earning rental income from tenants she has rented the bedrooms at the back of the house to, something we confirmed with this tenant before he was told not to speak to us any further.

Sound Up
Man: I’m renting there.

Producer: Oh you were renting there?

Man: Yes.

Producer: And this is some of your stuff that’s been thrown out here now?

Man: Yes

Voice
The man was visibly upset about being evicted. We tried to give Zwane a right of reply, but she didn’t want to talk to us.

Sound Up
Zwane: I don’t want to talk to you, just ask that man who brought you here.

Producer: He told me.

Zwane: He told you what?

Producer: You don’t want to talk to us?

Zwane: Wena go and ask that man.


Voice
And neither did her supporters…

Sound Up Supporter
Woman: You don’t want to remove that camera to me? No I don’t want to give you any statement, remove that camera to me.

Sound Up Cilna
And unfortunately this is what landlord’s are faced with, eventually a landlord is burdened with paying for a private security company.

Link Derek
You might expect that low income tenants are likely to default on payments, but research shows that high income earners are just as much of a problem.

Voice
Michelle Dickens is the managing director of TPN Credit Bureau. They are Africa’s largest credit bureau specialising in vetting tenants for rental properties. And their data reveals some interesting facts about tenant payment behaviour.

Sound Up Michelle
TPN profiles data on tenants across five different rental value brackets. So our low end of the market, affordable housing below R3000 per month, and then our top end of the market above R25 000 a month. Those two segments of the market are the most challenging to collect rent from.

Voice
Czuba had a court ordered eviction successfully executed, but the loss of rental income and legal costs were an expensive learning curve.

Sound Up Caroline
Derek: Caroline, looking back, what has this cost you financially?

Caroline: I would say about between R250 000 and R300 000 rand in those 15 months.

Voice
To add insult to injury, Czuba says her tenant didn’t exactly seem to have fallen on hard times…

Sound Up Caroline
She had bottles of french champagne in my kitchen, she had her son at Crawford College, a 12 year old, and she enjoyed she said living there, because it was close for him to walk to school.







Voice
But at least she managed to get rid of her unwanted guest. With the fourth eviction finished at Sibisi’s home, the Sheriff and police left. But literally five minutes later the community had forced their way back into the property. We were able to get this footage as police stood idly by and watched. Instead of arresting anyone, they took Sibisi back to Orlando police station to lay a charge of trespassing, which he did. The police have referred the case to the NPA for a decision, but Sibisi isn’t holding his breath.

Sound Up Sibisi
And I haven’t got money to buy a house again like the one that I have there, and that’s it.

Voice
The Prevention of Illegal Eviction act was put in place to protect tenants from unscrupulous landlords, and Steyn agrees it is a valid and much needed piece of legislation. But she also wants it amended to provide more protection for landlords and home owners like Sibisi.

Sound Up Cilna
Where do we go? I’ve been to the legislator, I’ve been to the Dept of Human Settlements. I’ve emailed Herman Mashaba. I’ve begged for assistance from the police. And everytime I get to a dead end, and I have another wall and another wall.

Voice
Dickens says their data shows it’s a nationwide problem.

Sound Up Michelle
It happens in every suburb in South Africa, it can happen in any rental value in South Africa.

Voice
Meanwhile Sibisi says he’s lost all faith in the justice system, and doubts that he’ll ever be able to move into his home.

Sound Up Sibisi
You know we have got a very good constitution in South Africa, but when it comes to implementing, the very same people that are involved, they are not doing their job.

Voice
But Steyn says no matter how many doors are shut in her face, she’ll keep fighting.

Sound Up Cilna
The truth is at some stage there is going to be a bit of a gap in the wall, and if the gap doesn’t just appear I’ll politely ask the constitutional court to help me with the door.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Two oceans marathon winner Thulani Sibisi bought a house in Orlando in the same street where Walter Sisulu once lived. It was his dream to live out his last days next to where the famous SA icon once lived. But since buying his property four years ago, Thulani has never been able to occupy the home. A family member of the previous owner has occupied the house and refused to move. Despite four court ordered evictions, police have failed to keep the illegal tenants out. We accompanied Thulani, the Sherrif and Public order policing units to serve the fourth eviction. But the tenant gathered support from the local community, and was able to break back into the house the very same day, chasing away Thulani's private security firm and reoccupying the home. Police stood by and did nothing despite our camera's presence.
metadata.Summary: Thulani's plight highlights the failure of the justice system to protect homeowners once tenants illegally occupy a home. Meanwhile, homeowners from our previous story in Eveleigh Estate in Boksburg, which dealt with the same issue, have still not had any successes either. After our story aired, most of the houses forcefully evicted by members of the EFF were reoccupied by the same tenants. Even landlords in upmarket areas face similar battles. Michelle Dickens from the TPN Credit Bureau monitors tenant behaviour in SA. She says 10% of tenants in SA are more than 3 months in arrears in South Africa. According to their data, problem tenants are in two categories - low end tenants who pay rental of R3000 per month and less, and high end tenants, who pay rental of more than R12 000. She has provided us with a landlord, Caroline, who is willing to be interviewed on the battles she has faced in getting tenants evicted in Up market Johannesburg suburbs. I am just waiting for her to contact me back, but Michelle has confirmed she will do interview.
